titleStmt.title: Memorandum by the Minister-Counselor of Embassy in China (Butterworth) to General George C. Marshall

div.head: Memorandum by the Minister-Counselor of Embassy in China (Butterworth) to General George C. Marshall
div.p: The two attached memoranda state the cases for the railroad and cotton loans. The pros and cons of these loans are summarized below:

list.label: a)
list.item: It is a long-term rehabilitation project vital for the restoration of Chinese communications and for the revival of the Chinese economy after the cessation of current hostilities.
list.label: b)
list.item: Because it is a long-term project, it is not open to the objection that it is a political loan of assistance to the National Government in the civil war, and is therefore readily defensible in terms of the President’s statement of December 15 [18], It should also be possible to impose conditions preventing abuse or misuse of equipment purchased with the loan.
list.label: c)
list.item: The railroad runs through an area in which there are no hostilities and little likelihood thereof. It is therefore unlikely that the investment in equipment and installations will be dissipated.

list.label: a)
list.item: The railroad has already been abused by the Military, and it may be difficult to prevent the recurrence of such abuses or the diversion of equipment intended for its rehabilitation to other railroads in areas of hostilities.
list.label: b)
list.item: The record of Chinese utilization of UNRRA railroad equipment is not impressive.
list.label: c)
list.item: The prospects for the repayment of the loan cannot be considered too bright.

list.label: a)
list.item: The cotton textile industry is China’s major industry, which moreover is functioning with relative efficiency. Its continued large-scale operation is vital to the prevention of further economic (and political) deterioration in Shanghai and in Nationalist China generally.
list.label: b)
list.item: The functioning of the cotton industry is not immediately related to the civil war.
list.label: c)
list.item: China can export some of her cotton manufactures and allocate the proceeds to the servicing and partial repayment of the loan.

list.label: a)
list.item: While a cotton loan would provide immediate relief, it would not contribute to any basic long-term improvement in the Chinese economy.
list.label: b)
list.item: Precisely because the cotton loan would provide immediate economic relief and improve the Government’s immediate financial position (the Government anticipates receiving CN$400 billion from the profits of the China Textile Development Corporation), it would be of assistance to the Government in waging civil war.
list.label: c)
list.item: While the foreign exchange proceeds of cotton textile exports could contribute to the servicing and partial repayment of the loan, it is improbable that they would be on a scale sufficient to ensure its full repayment.
